posts.mainText: UN announced a 40-member Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, selected from 2600 applicants across 140 countries, to deliver evidence-based assessments of AI risks and impacts.
posts.replyText: Bolsters global AI governance legitimacy by incorporating diverse perspectives, enabling coordinated international policy through scientific evidence on safety and societal effects.

posts.mainText: Vitalik Buterin warned AI safety efforts risk losing global credibility if tied to specific companies or countries attempting tech dominance.
posts.replyText: Highlights legitimacy challenges in AI safety coordination, urging broad, neutral approaches to maintain trust across institutions and avoid perceptions of power grabs.

posts.mainText: OECD released guidance for organizations to shape AI governance frameworks, integrating principles like fairness, risk assessment, monitoring, and remediation into existing compliance systems.
posts.replyText: Promotes institutional coordination by aligning enterprise AI practices with international standards, enhancing cross-org legitimacy through standardized risk management.

posts.mainText: Analysis calls for institutional governance of autonomous AI agents via mandatory safety benchmarks, independent audits, autonomy levels, liability rules, and international norms.
posts.replyText: Addresses coordination gaps by advocating US-led global standards and regulations, crucial for cross-organization safety efforts amid rising agentic AI risks.
